query: How can we reduce declined expense submissions?

per_column.name: missing_source_id
per_column.rationale: Whether a submission is missing a source_id is a settable data-quality property of the submission; an actor could enforce that source_id is provided, making it an intervenable lever plausibly affecting decline.

per_column.name: amount_bracket
per_column.rationale: Amount is largely determined by the underlying expense and drives decline risk; it is an intrinsic attribute rather than a lever one would set to reduce declines, and it can act as a common cause across submission types. Treated here as a covariate/confounder, not a true intervenable treatment.

per_column.name: processing_lag_days
per_column.rationale: Processing lag is measured relative to processing/decision events (values like -1 suggest it is defined post-outcome). It is downstream of or contemporaneous with the decision, so it behaves as a mediator/collider rather than a pre-treatment confounder.

per_column.name: user_decline_rate
per_column.rationale: An aggregate of the outcome itself (historical decline rate per user). Being a function of the outcome, it is a leakage/proxy feature, not a clean confounder or intervenable treatment.

per_column.name: category_decline_rate
per_column.rationale: Aggregated outcome rate by category; encodes the outcome and is not an intervenable lever nor a proper pre-treatment confounder.

per_column.name: department_decline_rate
per_column.rationale: Aggregated outcome rate by department; a mechanical outcome-derived summary, not a confounder of a treatment nor a settable lever.

judge.rationale: The query is explicitly interventional ('How can we reduce...'). Only missing_source_id qualifies as a genuinely intervenable treatment (a data-quality requirement an actor can enforce). However, the schema does not set up a proper causal design around it: the decline-rate columns (user/category/department) are aggregates of the OUTCOME itself, which are leakage-style features rather than confounders, and processing_lag_days is post-decision (mediator/collider). Only amount_bracket serves as a plausible, not-named-in-query confounder, and even it is a weak, generic covariate. No confounder was identified that is a common cause of the missing_source_id treatment specifically. The set therefore only weakly realises the what-if claim: a lever is present, but confounder adjustment for that lever is essentially absent.
